$schema_note: Declarative allowlist of runtime files that app.py's _LIVE_STATIC_ELIGIBLE_FILES (app.py, ~line 17721) or an explicitly routed subpath permits to be served from the live-static override root (GO_ODYSSEY_LIVE_STATIC_ROOT / /opt/go-odyssey-static/current) before falling back to the file baked into the Docker image. This file is the single tracked source of truth for the static release tooling's eligible paths; root-level entries remain synchronized with app.py and explicitly routed subpath assets are listed here when they are required in a generation.

eligible_files.description: Every repository-relative file path the static release tooling may stage. Root-level entries mirror app.py's flat live-static allowlist; explicitly routed subpath assets are included when the application serves them through the live-static-aware subpath contract. Not all eligible files are part of every static release generation -- see required_in_generation below.

required_in_generation.description: The subset of eligible_files this Sprint's static release tooling (scripts/release/package-static-release.ps1 / deploy-static-release.ps1) actually stages, ships, and verifies in every generation. i18n.js and sw.js remain governed because they were observed stale in live-static. index.html is governed because an older live-static entrypoint can mask the exact app image's shell wiring. site-nav.js, js/map_battle_v1_adapter.js, and js/game/lord_trial_controller.js are required because index.html references these exact application assets. js/e9/shell.js remains required with the E10 shell navigation owner. The runtime_dependency_closure below derives the E10 JS/CSS/component closure from index.html and the shell's component references. Other eligible pages remain intentionally baked-image fallback content and are outside this focused contract.

runtime_dependency_closure.description: The E10 client closure is derived from the index.html entrypoint and recursively resolved local references. Declared subtrees are the live-static-routed E9 runtime boundary; every referenced file must exist in the exact source checkout and is staged with its SHA-256 and size.

required_subtrees.description: RELEASE-FIX-A2 (see docs/incidents/2026-07-12-full-site-asset-outage.md): RELEASE-FIX-A's narrow i18n.js/sw.js-only scope left assets/ management to whatever the production host happened to have mounted -- an undocumented, untracked 757MB tree that RELEASE-FIX-A's own generation switch silently orphaned, breaking every image on the site. assets/ is no longer excluded_prefixes; it is now release-bound and generation-managed, staged from the declarative closure manifests below -- NOT by copying an entire directory tree wholesale (that reintroduces exactly the untracked-content problem this fixes). RELEASE-FIX-A3 superseded the original 180-file runtime-reference-derived closure with the complete verified historical image pack (1,298 files) -- a runtime reference scan proved to be an incomplete ownership boundary (query-string and dynamically-constructed paths were invisible to it; see docs/incidents/2026-07-12-full-site-asset-outage.md's RELEASE-FIX-A3 addendum). Reference scanning remains a regression/observability layer (tests/test_release_fix_a2_asset_closure.py), not the source of truth for what ships. A second, narrower entry was added for assets/storyboards/*.mp3 narration audio (2026-07-15) -- canonical-image-pack-manifest.json is validated image/*-MIME-only (test_manifest_contains_only_image_mime_types) and its own $schema_note documents deliberately excluding these 90 files, so a companion audio-specific closure manifest governs them instead of weakening the image contract. Dedicated E10 Zone 1 and Zone 2 media entries keep Owner-locked namespaces separate from the historical image pack and storyboard narration audio.

entries.staging_rule: Stage exactly the files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Never stage a file under assets/ that is not in this manifest, even if present on disk -- a partial or over-broad generation must fail closed (see package-static-release.ps1 and its tests).

Stage exactly the files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Never stage a file under assets/storyboards/ that is not in this manifest, even if present on disk -- a partial or over-broad generation must fail closed (see package-static-release.ps1 and its tests). Deliberately disjoint from the image manifest above (zero *.mp3 entries there, zero non-audio entries here) -- no path is staged twice.

Stage exactly the files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Never stage an E10 Zone 1 audio file that is not in this manifest, even if present on disk -- a partial or over-broad generation must fail closed. This namespace is disjoint from the storyboard audio pack and the image pack.

Stage exactly the ten Owner-selected Zone 2 WebP files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Never stage a Zone 2 storyboard file that is not in this manifest. This namespace is disjoint from the historical image pack by file membership.

Stage exactly the six Owner-attached Zone 2 Lord Trial WebP files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Canonical JPEG source evidence is never staged. This namespace is disjoint from the historical image pack and the Zone 2 storyboard pack.

Stage exactly the twenty-three Owner-locked bilingual Zone 2 audio files listed in the manifest's `files` array, at their declared `path`, verified against their declared `sha256`. Never stage an E10 Zone 2 audio file that is not in this manifest. This namespace is disjoint from Zone 1 audio and storyboard narration audio.

excluded_prefixes.description: Subdirectory trees app.py also serves live-static-aware (via _serve_live_static_or_baked_subpath), still OUT OF SCOPE -- externally-versioned content with its own separate lifecycle (see Dockerfile's 'Content and asset boundary' comment), not git-tracked application code with a canonical source commit. assets/ was moved to required_subtrees above by RELEASE-FIX-A2; icons/ remains excluded (no current runtime reference resolves to it).

forbidden_patterns.description: Defense-in-depth reject list enforced by the static release tooling, independent of the allowlist check above -- even a typo'd or maliciously-crafted eligible_files entry could never pass these.
